title: S3 Lifecycle and CORS
description: Apply lifecycle policies for cost management and configure CORS for browser-based uploads.

data.text: S3 lifecycle policies automate moving objects between storage classes and deleting old files. CORS configuration allows browser-based apps to upload directly to S3.
Lifecycle rules can transition objects to cheaper storage classes after a certain age and delete them when they are no longer needed.

data.title: Apply a lifecycle policy with AWS CLI
data.content: Create a JSON policy and apply it to the bucket.

data.text: When browsers upload files directly to S3, the bucket must allow cross-origin requests from your ASP.NET Core app domain.

data.title: Configure CORS on an S3 bucket
data.content: Use the AWS CLI to set CORS rules.

data.title: CORS and presigned URLs
data.text: Presigned URLs bypass CORS because the request is made directly to S3 with the signature. CORS is required for browser-based uploads using the S3 JavaScript SDK.

data.title: Add lifecycle and CORS to the demo bucket
data.description: Automate storage costs and enable browser uploads.
steps: Create a lifecycle policy that moves uploads to Standard-IA after 30 days
Create a CORS rule allowing your app origin
Upload a test file and verify it respects the lifecycle
Attempt a browser upload from localhost and confirm it succeeds
data.expectedOutcome: The bucket automatically manages object storage classes and allows cross-origin uploads.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Lifecycle policies reduce storage costs automatically
Transition objects to cheaper classes based on age
Presigned URLs do not require CORS
data.takeaway: Combine lifecycle policies for cost control and CORS for browser uploads to build a complete S3 storage solution.
